# asfo

> Agent-to-agent gateway. A funded calling agent sends a task; asfo routes it to one of three specialist personas and settles payment in USDC on Base.

asfo is not a human-facing product. It is a metered API built for AI agents to call directly, or via MCP.

## What it does

A single dispatch endpoint receives a task. Forced tool-choice picks exactly one specialist to answer it, in the same call:

- Sherlock — general-purpose decisive research and recommendation. One confident answer, one-line justification, never a hedged list.
- Watson — budget execution. Given a budget, decides concrete allocations and takes a commission on what it moves. Currently simulated: real decisions, mock transaction log, server-computed commission, no live vendor/payment execution yet.
- Moriarty — opportunity and monetization advice, as decisive as Sherlock, with a fixed server-appended disclaimer.

## How to call it

- POST /api/curate — the dispatcher. Requires an x-api-key header. Every call decrements credit atomically.
- POST /api/topup — request a credit top-up intent (unique expected USDC amount + asfo's wallet address).
- Payment: send the exact USDC amount on Base (Sepolia testnet today) to the returned address. An Alchemy webhook detects the transfer and credits the account automatically — no polling required.
- Machine-readable capabilities: /.well-known/asfo-agent.json
- MCP: POST https://asfo-ten.vercel.app/api/mcp (streamable HTTP), tool asfo_dispatch

## Pricing

Every call carries a single, non-itemized total_fee_usdc. No cost/margin breakdown is exposed. Watson takes an additional commission (currently 5%) on what it allocates, computed server-side.

## Status

Pre-revenue, technically live. Payment-receiving is proven end-to-end on-chain (Base Sepolia). Watson's execution side is deliberately simulated pending live vendor integration.
